newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-FREE STATE CONFIRMED AS SUPER 12 ENTRANTS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-FREE STATE CONFIRMED AS SUPER 12 ENTRANTS.

text.p: Free State will join defending Currie Cup champions Natal, Transvaal and Northern Transvaal as South Africa's representatives in next year's Super 12 tournament, it was confirmed on Friday.

The South African Rugby Football Union (SARFU) have stuck with the original plan of selecting the four semifinalists in this year's Currie Cup competition, resisting any temptation to reinstate Western Province, traditionally one of the country's strongest and richest provinces.
SARFU also announced that, in future, provincial players will be able to transfer between teams both in and out of season.
Transfers will be negotiated between the buying and the selling unions, with any player not contracted to a provincial rugby union permitted to act as a free agent.

The new system, effective from the end of the month, allows a player who has not asked for a transfer to receive 10 percent of the transfer fee. In contrast, a player who does request a move is not entitled to a percentage. The SARFU executive committee also considered copying the New Zealand policy of drafting players into different provincial teams for Super 12 matches.
"A draft system is being considered but will not be implemented until its feasibility has been closely examined," said a spokesman.
